reason: 2.1.1 gives nav details.dropdown a negative vertical margin of --femto-nav-element-spacing-vertical. Where <details> honors display: inline, as it does since the details layout change that also brought ::details-content (Chrome 131, Firefox 143, Safari 18.4), that margin does nothing. Firefox 128 to 142, including ESR 128 and 140, lays <details> out as a block container even when it is inline, and there the margin lifted every nav dropdown 2.5 to 2.75px above the nav links beside it, with its text 3.5 to 4.25px above theirs; it also shortened the nav and pulled a dropdown in an aside nav up against the item above it. femto sets the margin to 0, so the dropdown lines up with the links there, and where the details is inline only the computed margin changes.
notes: Fixtures: the nav dropdowns of the six pages in where.pages (kitchen-sink.html's header nav, the "Nav dropdown" and role=button nav dropdown of classes-dropdown.html, both open nav dropdowns of classes-dropdown-open.html, components-nav.html, layout-elements.html and components-tooltip.html); the margin goes from -16px at 390 and -20px at 1280 to 0px in every cell. The lift itself needs the old details layout, which no harness browser has, so it was probed with a standalone Selenium page at 1300, 1100, 700 and 400px (roots of 20, 19, 17 and 16px), ltr and rtl, light and dark. In Firefox 160 beta with layout.details.force-block-layout=true (Gecko's switch for the pre-143 layout), the summary box sat 2.75, 2.7, 2.56 and 2.5px above the link, the nav was 78.5, 74.63, 66.88 and 63px tall instead of 90, 85.5, 76.5 and 72, and an aside dropdown sat 1.5 to 1px below the link above it instead of 10 to 8px; with margin 0 every box matches the shipped layout. In Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta as shipped, no box moves. Chromium before 131 and Safari before 18.4 were not tested and may also lay details out as a block container. In Chrome 158 with display: inline-block forced on the details, as an emulation of such an engine, 2.1.1 set the summary box 1 to 1.5px below the links, shortened the nav to 70, 66.5, 59.5 and 56px and left an aside gap of 1.5 to 1px; with the fix the summary box is level with the links, the nav keeps its height and the aside gaps are restored, exactly as in the current-browser layout. With display: block forced, 2.1.1 lifted the summary 15.5 to 19.25px and the fix lines it up. Upstream issue picocss/pico#498.

reason: 2.1.1 pads the fixed-height nav summary with the nav link spacing minus two border widths, which leaves one border width of extra space under the text, so the summary text sat one border width (1 to 1.5px at femto's root sizes) above the text of the nav links beside it. femto subtracts one border width, so the content box holds exactly one line and the text and chevron line up with the links. The summary box keeps its size and position, and a summary with role=button keeps its padding.
notes: Fixtures: the plain nav summaries of the six pages in where.pages; the vertical padding goes from 6px to 7px at 390 and from 7.5px to 8.75px at 1280. Probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 1300, 1100, 700 and 400px, ltr and rtl, light and dark: the summary text sat 1.5, 1.37, 1.12 and 1px above the link text, and with the fix 0.25, 0.19, 0.06 and 0px (sub-pixel, as the border paints at a snapped 1px), with the same box. The same holds with Firefox's pre-143 details layout once nav-dropdown-no-negative-margin lines the box up. In the harness the pixel differences fall inside the summaries, apart from the 390px cells where a label wraps and the chevron on its second line, below the summary box, sits one border width lower. Upstream issue picocss/pico#498.

reason: 2.1.1 sets nav details.dropdown to display: inline, so the details is an inline box split around its block summary, and that split box is the containing block of the absolutely positioned list. Firefox 143 and later place the list against an empty fragment of it (nav-dropdown-open-list-placement). femto makes the details a block, which with its zero margin fills the nav item exactly as the summary did, so the details box is the list's containing block. Every browser now reports display: block and the details' used width, height, inline-size and block-size, with transform and perspective origins at its center, where the inline box reported auto and 0px 0px. A nav dropdown that is the only content of its nav item keeps its closed, hover, focus and open layout in Chrome and Firefox 143 and later.
notes: Fixtures: the nav dropdowns of the six pages in where.pages, closed (kitchen-sink.html's header nav, classes-dropdown.html, components-nav.html, layout-elements.html, components-tooltip.html) and open (classes-dropdown-open.html). In the harness only these values of the details change; every other element keeps its computed style. A standalone Selenium page in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 1000 and 400px, ltr and rtl, closed, open and opened by a real click, measured the rects of the summary, nav item, nav and neighbouring links equal before and after for a plain summary, a role=button summary and a dropdown in an aside nav. What changes outside the harness fixtures, measured on the same page: (1) A dropdown wrapped in a <label> inside a nav now takes label > details.dropdown's top margin of a quarter of --femto-spacing, as outside a nav, in Chrome and Firefox 143 and later, where the inline details ignored it: the summary moves down 4.5px at 1000px and 4px at 400px, and the nav item and the nav grow by as much. (2) When text precedes the dropdown in its nav item ('Theme: <details>'), Chrome placed the open list against the first inline fragment, 60.63px right of the summary at 1000px in ltr and 12.11px short of its end in rtl; it now lines up under the summary in Chrome and Firefox. (3) data-tooltip on the nav dropdown's <details> (not its summary) now draws the tooltip's 1px dotted bottom border under the summary, as a dropdown outside a nav already does, and the nav item is 1px taller (90 to 91px at 1280) in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160; in Firefox 160 the tooltip bubble also moves from the corner of an empty fragment (left 0px, bottom -1px) to over the summary. (4) Firefox 128 to 142 lay details out as a block container even when it is inline, which behaves like an inline-block; probed in Firefox 160 beta with layout.details.force-block-layout=true at 1280 and 500px, the open lists were already placed correctly there, and with the fix a dropdown in an aside nav fills its item as in Chrome and newer Firefox (summary 189.88 to 1200px at 1280, 155.92 to 468px at 500), and text before a nav dropdown in the same item sits on its own line (nav 90 to 120px at 1280, 72 to 96px at 500); a dropdown that is the only content of its nav item does not move. Chromium before 131 and Safari before 18.4 may behave like old Firefox and were not tested. Safari was not probed for this change. Upstream issues picocss/pico#701 and picocss/pico#671.

reason: Consequence of nav-dropdown-block-details in Safari's computed style only. The dropdown is position: relative with every inset auto, so it does not move. Safari's getComputedStyle reports the insets of a relatively positioned inline box as auto but those of a block as their used value, 0px, so the details changing from inline to block changes what Safari reports. Chrome and Firefox report the same value for both, so they show no difference.
notes: Seen in Safari 27.2 on a dark OS in every leg it runs, ltr and rtl, at 390 and 1280, at rest and in every state, on the nav details.dropdown elements of the six pages (three on classes-dropdown-open.html, two on classes-dropdown.html, one on each of the others), with auto in the reference and 0px in femto for all eight properties. Pixel differences on those pages match Chrome's and Firefox's within a few pixels, so the dropdowns render in the same place.

selector: nav details.dropdown[open] > summary + ul, nav details.dropdown[open] > summary + ul li, nav details.dropdown[open] > summary + ul li a
reason: Consequence of nav-dropdown-block-details. With 2.1.1's inline nav details, Firefox 143 and later place the open list against an empty fragment beside the summary instead of the summary's box: a right-aligned list (ul dir=rtl) ends at the summary's left edge and hangs over the neighbouring link, a left-aligned list shrinks to its items, and in an rtl page a left-aligned list starts at the summary's right edge. With the details a block, the list lines up under the summary at its width, as in Chrome, so the list's resolved insets, its width and the widths and origins of its items and links change. picocss/pico#671 reports the same misplacement of a dir=rtl list in Safari 18.4.
notes: Fixtures: the two open nav dropdowns of classes-dropdown-open.html, both with ul dir=rtl, and the open nav dropdown with a left aligned list below them. In Firefox 160 beta at 1280 the role=button summary's list goes from left -80.37px and 80.37px wide to left 0px and 287.82px wide, and the left-aligned list from right -80.37px and 80.37px wide to right 0px and 415.12px wide; at 390 the lists go from 65.77 and 88.97px to 184.32, 143.82 and 343.3px wide. A standalone Selenium page at 1000 and 400px, ltr and rtl, open by attribute and by a real click, measured list minus summary edges: in Firefox 160 beta before the fix, with the reference and with femto alike, a dir=rtl list at 1000px in an ltr page was -99.18 / -178.42px (99.18px wide under a 178.42px summary), a left-aligned list 0 / -121.85px (99.18px under 221.03px), a list in an aside nav 99.18px under 700px, and in an rtl page a left-aligned list started 221.04px right of the summary's left edge; after the fix every case is 0 / 0 at the summary's width, and the pixel 8px under the summary is the dropdown background instead of the page. Chrome Beta 158 is 0 / 0 before and after, so this entry leaves it out. Safari was not probed; it is listed because picocss/pico#671 reports the dir=rtl list aligned to the summary's left edge in Safari 18.4 (macOS 15.4, iOS 18.4). Upstream issues picocss/pico#701 and picocss/pico#671.

reason: 2.1.1 pads every dropdown li, and a checkbox or radio label alone in its li sits inside that padding with the global label rule's bottom margin of 0.375 * --femto-spacing below it. The whole li highlights on hover, but the label covered only its middle, so a click in the side or top padding or in the bottom strip hit the li and did not toggle the input. femto keeps the li's padding and lets a label that is the li's only element reach over it, as link rows already do: negative margins of the row padding, the same padding on the label, and the former bottom margin added to its bottom padding. The label's border box is now the row, so its computed width, height, inline and block sizes, margins, paddings and transform and perspective origins change, and its cursor covers the whole row. For a label holding its input and text, the row size, the input and text positions, the hover color and the painted pixels do not change. A lone label whose last child is a block with a bottom margin, such as a field with a <small> helper, makes its row taller by 0.375 * --femto-spacing, since that margin no longer collapses through the label. :only-child ignores text nodes, so an li with bare text beside its only label element also matches; the li keeps its padding there and the text does not move. Rows where the label sits beside its input (input + label for) or beside other elements keep 2.1.1's layout.
notes: Fixtures: the three label rows of "Open dropdown with checkboxes and radios" in classes-dropdown-open.html (the first with data-states="hover") and the two label rows of the dropdown inside a label in classes-dropdown.html; at 390 the label goes from 356x24 to 388x42 with margins -6px -16px and padding 6px 16px 12px, at 1280 from 1238x30 to 1278x52.5 with margins -7.5px -20px and padding 7.5px 20px 15px, and no li or list changes. Probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta, light and dark, at 1000 and 420 wide, with checkbox, checked checkbox, radio and switch rows in ltr, ul dir=rtl, div dir=rtl, data-theme light and dark islands and a nav dropdown: before the fix the label covered 46 to 58 percent of the li on a 2px elementFromPoint grid and real pointer clicks at the inline-start, inline-end, top and bottom padding toggled nothing (21 of 105, center only); after it the label box equals the li box (698x47.25 at 1000, 466x42 at 420), coverage is 100 percent, 105 of 105 clicks toggle and the cursor on the former padding is pointer. The li, input and text rects, the hover background and the link, plain text, sibling label and nested label rows are unchanged; Firefox screenshots are pixel-identical, and Chrome's few differing pixels (channel delta up to 10) fall within the run-to-run noise it shows between the reference and the unchanged femto sheet. Edge cases on the same browsers: a label followed or preceded by bare text keeps the text where 2.1.1 puts it, pixel-identical; a label ending in an input with a <small> helper grows its row by 6.75px at 1000 and 6px at 420. Upstream issue picocss/pico#691.

reason: 2.1.1 floats a dropdown's chevron right in every direction: its rule outranks the accordion's [dir=rtl] float. So in right-to-left text the chevron sat on the start side, against the label, while a <select> next to it has its chevron on the left. femto floats it to the inline end, so in right-to-left text the chevron sits on the left like a select's, with the offset mirrored (dropdown-chevron-rtl-offset). In left-to-right text nothing moves, but getComputedStyle reports inline-end instead of right.
notes: Seen in run fixes-full-1 (Chrome 158, Firefox 161) on every dropdown summary, and on the link and button children of the open dropdown in classes-dropdown.html. Measured with standalone Selenium pages at an 18px root, against the built dist: in rtl a form dropdown's chevron was 24px from the right border with 2.1.1 (23px in Firefox), and is now 20px from the left border (19px in Firefox), the mirror of its place in ltr; a select's chevron is 19px from the left border.

reason: 2.1.1 nudges a dropdown's chevron 0.2rem toward the end edge with translateX(0.2rem), a physical shift to the right. With the chevron on the left in right-to-left text (dropdown-chevron-float-inline-end), that shift would move it toward the label, so femto mirrors it to translateX(-0.2rem) there. The chevron then sits as far from the left border in right-to-left text as from the right border in left-to-right text, about as far as a select's chevron. A nav dropdown's chevron has no shift, as in 2.1.1.
notes: Seen in run fixes-full-1 (Chrome 158, Firefox 161) on the dropdown summaries, links and buttons in right-to-left text: in the rtl legs of classes-dropdown.html, classes-dropdown-open.html and kitchen-sink.html, and in the dir=rtl blocks of the first two in their ltr legs. The shift is 0.2rem at the root size of each width (3.2px to 4.2px).
